It is also estimated that an additional 5.26 million pounds of aluminum will be used as a substitute material for vehicle weight reduction. This is 0.055 percent of total national consumption of aluminum of 9.6 billion pounds in 1975. The increased use of aluminum will result in a one-time additional consumption of energy equivalent in BTU's to 100,000 barrels of oil which is 0.002 percent of total national consumption in 1975. Thus, under this viewpoint this action is likely to result in an increase (15,000 barrels of oil equivalent) in the amount of energy required to manufacture these vehicles. However, this amount is insignificant compared to the energy saving (18.14 to 29.7 million barrels of oil equivalent) in the operation of these vehicles due to their increased fuel economy. The increased use of plastics and aluminum could result in a small deterioration in water quality, a small increase in industrial water supply demand, and a small increase in stationary source air pollution resulting from increased production. However, since the increased use of plastics and aluminum is only 0.025 percent and 0.055 percent, respectively, of their total national consumption, these latter impacts should be minor.
